EAACI Molecular Allergology User's Guide 2.0; Since the discovery of immunoglobulin E (IgE) as a mediator of allergic diseases in 1967, our knowledge about the immunological mechanisms of IgE-mediated allergies has remarkably increased. In addition to understanding the immune response and clinical symptoms, allergy diagnosis and management depend strongly on the precise identification of the elicitors of the IgE-mediated allergic reaction. In the past four decades, innovations in bioscience and technology have facilitated the identification and production of well-defined, highly pure molecules for component-resolved diagnosis (CRD), allowing a personalized diagnosis and management of the allergic disease for individual patients. The first edition of the “EAACI Molecular Allergology User's Guide” (MAUG) in 2016 rapidly became a key reference for clinicians, scientists, and interested readers with a background in allergology, immunology, biology, and medicine. Nevertheless, the field of molecular allergology is moving fast, and after 6 years, a new EAACI Taskforce was established to provide an updated document. The Molecular Allergology User's Guide 2.0 summarizes state-of-the-art information on allergen molecules, their clinical relevance, and their application in diagnostic algorithms for clinical practice. It is designed for both, clinicians and scientists, guiding health care professionals through the overwhelming list of different allergen molecules available for testing. Further, it provides diagnostic algorithms on the clinical relevance of allergenic molecules and gives an overview of their biology, the basic mechanisms of test formats, and the application of tests to measure allergen exposure.

This consensus document, which included the participation of 87 primary authors and 40 additional consultant authors, who critically appraised evidence on 144 individual topics concerning allergic rhinitis, provides guidance for health care providers using the evidence-based review with recommendations (EBRR) methodology. This synopsis highlights topical areas including pathophysiology, epidemiology, disease burden, risk and protective factors, evaluation and diagnosis, aeroallergen avoidance and environmental controls, single and combination pharmacotherapy options, allergen immunotherapy (subcutaneous, sublingual, rush, cluster), pediatric considerations, alternative and emerging therapies, and unmet needs. Based on the EBRR methodology, ICAR:AR includes strong recommendations for the treatment of allergic rhinitis: (1) for the use of newer generation antihistamines compared with first-generation alternatives, intranasal corticosteroid, intranasal saline, combination therapy with intranasal corticosteroid plus intranasal antihistamine for patients not responding to monotherapy, and subcutaneous immunotherapy and sublingual tablet immunotherapy in properly selected patients

Anaphylaxis is Uncommon in Clinical Trials of Sublingual Immunotherapy Tablets as Identified by a Standardized Algorithm; Rationale: There is no universal consensus definition for anaphylaxis in sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) trials. Therefore, the reported incidence varies considerably. An algorithm in the Standardized MedDRA Query (SMQ) was used to identify anaphylaxis in SLIT-tablet trials. Methods: Criteria 1 of the algorithm was treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) with narrow MedDRA preferred terms representing anaphylaxis (i.e., “anaphylactic reaction”). Criteria 2 was all TEAEs with broad terms from ≥2 of 3 categories (respiratory, skin, and cardiovascular) occurring on the same day. The criteria were applied to all subjects in 43 clinical trials (all phases) receiving approved SLIT-tablet doses or placebo. Identified cases were adjudicated (blinded to treatment) by medical professionals and were considered anaphylaxis if either criteria were met and included investigator-assessed severe respiratory or cardiovascular compromise. Results: For grass SLIT-tablet, 1 case of treatment-related anaphylaxis was identified in 3984 active-treated subjects and no cases were identified in 2743 placebo-treated subjects. For ragweed SLIT-tablet, 1 case of treatment-related anaphylaxis was identified in 894 active-treated subjects and 1 case was identified in 892 placebo-treated subjects. For HDM and tree SLIT-tablets combined, no cases of treatment-related anaphylaxis were identified in a total of 2646 active-treated and 3024 placebo-treated subjects. The overall incidence rates in active- and placebo-treated subjects were 0.03% (2/7524) and 0.02% (1/6659), respectively. Neither anaphylaxis case associated with active treatment was life-threatening. Conclusions: The applied SMQ algorithm provides reproducible identification of anaphylaxis that can be applied to SLIT trials and possibly to real-world data. Anaphylaxis was uncommon for SLIT-tablets across the evaluated allergens.

Extract-shaped immune repertoire as source for nanobody-based human IgE in grass pollen allergy; Background: A llergens a re d efined by t heir r eactivity w ith I gE a ntibodies of allergic patients. In contrast to the complex heterotetrameric canonical antibodies, the adaptive immune system of i.a. camelid species has evolved heavy chain only antibodies for antigen recognition. Derived single domain antibodies, or nanobodies (nb), represent a versatile platform for the development of diagnostic tools and concepts, in particular for antigens available in purified form. In this study we evaluated the feasibility of obtaining nanobody-based tools using timothy grass pollen as target. Method: A library from pollen extract immunised llamas was selected by phage display against the extract and resulting nanobodies were characterised for the binding specificity. Potential antigens in the pollen extract were identified by immunoblotting and subsequent immunoCAP analyses. Nanobody-based IgE antibodies were generated by fusion of nanobodies to human IgE Fc, produced in mammalian cells and assessed in different immunoassay formats and commercial platforms. Results: The library selection yielded nanobodies secreted into bacterial supernatant with immunoreactivity to grass pollen extract. Immunoblotting documented the specificity for an approx. 10-12 kDa allergen in the pollen extract. Human, bivalent nb-IgE derivatives were obtained from mammalian cells in high yields. Profiling by Immunocap analysis on candidate allergens identified the major pollen allergen Phl p 6 as target. Further analysis with group 5/6 allergens from different grasses provided additional insights into molecular cross-reactivity. Upon sensitization with nb-IgE, activation of effector cells documented the capability for FcϵRI-mediated degranulation. Conclusion: Our study shows that extract-based immunisation enables the generation of allergen-specific nb-IgE formats linking nanobody technologies with allergological applications. Furthermore, our data provides proof of concept for use as standardisation tool in grass pollen allergy with implications for diagnostic and immunotherapeutic concepts.
MicroRNA expression in patients with allergic rhinitis during grass pollen immunotherapy; Background: Subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) is a well-established method of treatment of allergic rhinitis (AR) resulting in symptoms and pharmacotherapy reduction, and better quality of life. However, mechanisms of allergen tolerance induction during SCIT have not been fully understood. miRNAs are important epigenetic mechanism of regulating gene expression and may play a significant role in the process of regaining tolerance. The aim of this study was to determine expression of 48 selected miRNAs in patients with AR undergoing SCIT with grass pollen and find relations between miRNAs profile and clinical outcome. Method: The study group comprised 16 adult patients with AR related to grass pollen allergy, including 13 patients undergoing SCIT. The control group was comprised of seven healthy adult subjects. Expression of 48 miRNAs was determined by means of RT PCR in the full blood of all study participants. Severity of AR and response to SCIT were assessed with Allergy Control Score. Results: Out of 48 miRNAs three (miR-136, miR-208 and miR-190) were upregulated in AR group in comparison with controls (p < 0.05). After 6 months of SCIT we found significant downregulation of proinflammatory miR-146a, miR-498, miR-22, miR-155 and upregulation of several miRNAs playing a role in regulating Th1/Th2 balance (miR-625, miR-1248, miR-513- 5p). Moreover, expression of miR-208, miR-136 and miR-190 after 6 months of immunotherapy did not differ from healthy controls any longer. Compared to AR patients treated symptomatically, SCIT group was characterized by lower expression of miR-136 and miR-483- 5p. No differences have been found in miRNAs expression between good and poor responders. Conclusion: This study has led to better understanding of epigenetic mechanisms of the subcutaneous immunotherapy with grass pollens by demonstrating some changes in the miRNAs expression during the treatment. However no single miRNA was found to be associated with clinical efficacy of AIT.

Compensation of micronutritional deficiencies in immune cells of allergic patients leads to significant improvement in combined symptom and medication score (CSMS) in a double-blind placebo-controlled pilot study; Background: Functional iron deficiency facilitates allergy development and potentially amplifies the symptom burden in allergy sufferers. It was previously shown that micronutrients can selectively be delivered to immune cells with beta-lactoglobulin as carrier (holoBLG), resulting in immune resilience, symptom relief and allergy prevention. Allergen immunotherapy is the only causative treatment for allergic diseases like hay fever and clinical studies focus on the combined symptom and medication score (CSMS, as recommended by the European Academy for Allergy and Clinical Immunology -EAACI) as primary endpoint readout. The EAACI CSMS was assessed in grass-and/ or birch-pollen- allergic women supplemented with a FSMP (food for special medical purpose) lozenge containing beta-lactoglobulin with iron, polyphenols, retinoic acid, and zinc (holoBLG lozenge) in a proof-of- concept study as secondary endpoint. Method: In a proof-of- concept, randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled study, grass-and/ or birch pollen allergic women (n = 51) were supplemented with holoBLG (verum) or placebo lozenges for 6 months in 2019 and 2020. Daily symptoms, medications, pollen concentrations and well-being were recorded by the patients in an eHealth application. These results were evaluated as recommended by the gold standard (CSMS) for allergen immunotherapy studies by the EAACI as secondary endpoint in this study. Results: CSMS during the birch peak and entire season as well as entire grass pollen season improved significantly in allergic subjects supplemented with the holoBLG lozenge by 45, 31 and 40% compared to the placebo arm. The daily symptom score dSS improved by 38.6% for the birch peak season, 35.2% for the entire birch season and 25.6% for the entire grass pollen season (all p < 0.0001). Conclusion: Targeted micronutrition with the holoBLG lozenge seemed effective in significantly reducing the symptom burden in allergic women. The extent in CSMS reduction in this pilot trial is comparable to the effects shown in trials for allergen immunotherapy products. The underlying allergen-independent mechanism provides evidence, that dietary nutritional supplementation of the immune system is one of many cornerstones to combat atopy.
Evaluation of the effect of allergen immunotherapy by clinical and biological markers in patients with allergic rhinitis in real life-first results from Bulgaria; Background: Allergen immunotherapy is a proven therapeutic approach for allergic rhinitis with/without asthma that leads to a significant reduction of symptoms, the need for pharmacotherapy as well as a considerable improvement of quality of life. However, the correlation between clinical and immunological biomarkers in evaluation of the effect of allergen immunotherapy is still not fully established. Our aim was to study the long-term effect of allergen immunotherapy in allergic rhinitis patients based on some clinical and immunological outcomes. Methods: Patients with allergic rhinitis at least two years after a three-year course of subcutaneous or sublingual allergen immunotherapy with either grass pollen or house dust mite were included. We assessed clinical outcomes by using specific questionnaires validated in Bulgarian language-rhinitis control-Rhinitis Control Assessment Test (RCAT), quality of life-Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire (RQLQ) as well as satisfaction with immunotherapy-Satisfaction Scale for Patients Receiving Allergen Immunotherapy (ESPIA). Specific IgG4 levels were measured by ImmunoCAP according to the EAACI position paper recommendations for monitoring clinical efficacy of allergen immunotherapy. Results: We included a total number of 69 patients (male 43, mean age 31.7 SD 12.04, age range 18-56). Allergic rhinitis was well controlled in 53 patients (76.47%). A good quality of life-overall score 0.65 (SD 0.78) and a high level of satisfaction 72.3 (SD 12.9) were found. Immunological examination of specific IgG4 antibodies by Immuno CAP revealed statistically significant higher levels of blocking antibodies in controlled patients than in uncontrolled (p < 0.05). Conclusion: Results confirm the key mechanism of allergen immunotherapy- formation of blocking allergen specific IgG4 antibodies with a long life even after treatment cessation. We highlight the long lasting immunological tolerance due to allergen immunotherapy and the correlation between immunological biomarkers and clinical outcomes.
Real-life effectiveness of mite, grass and pellitory injected AIT with monomeric carbamylated allergens; Background: Over the years, the efficacy and safety of both injected and sublingual Allergen Immunotherapy (AIT) has been widely documented trough clinical trials. Many reviews and meta-analyses support AIT as an effective and safe treatment for inhalant allergies. In recent years, the need of AIT real-life studies is emerging to counterbalance the difficulty to apply methods and patient selectivity of randomized clinical trials to patients in real-life clinical practice. Method: The present is a real-life retrospective cohort study (performed in Italy and Albania) evaluating the effectiveness, safety and patient satisfaction of inhalant (house dust mites, grass and pellitory) allergic patients suffering from rhinoconjunctivitis and/or asthma, treated for 3 consecutive years with monomeric allergoid injection immunotherapy. Perceived efficacy and satisfaction with AIT, ARIA classification of rhinitis, perceived impact of rhinitis and asthma, number of asthma worsening episodes and drug consumption were assessed using questionnaires relating to before, after one year, at the end of treatment and after one/two years AIT. Results: A total number of 291 patients (169 Albanian and 122 Italian) were enrolled. Patient's perception of AIT effectiveness, as assessed by symptom reduction after discontinuation versus initiation of treatment, was excellent. In fact, overall symptoms score associated to rhinoconjunctivitis and asthma evaluated by VAS significantly decreased over the years independently form specific sensitization (p < 0.01). All patients except seven reported a reduction in rhinitis, as classified by ARIA, from moderate-severe persistent to mild/intermittent. A significant reduction (p < 0.01) was observed in the use of antihistamines in rhinoconjunctivitis patients and in the need of bronchodilators in asthmatics. Interestingly, a significant reduction (p < 0.01) has been observed in the asthma worsening episodes needing the use of systemic steroids. No patient reported severe side effects and only few local oedema and pruritus in the injection site. Finally, in an overall assessment of treatment efficacy, 230 patients reported a complete satisfaction with treatment, 51 were satisfied, 5 very unhappy, 1 unsatisfied and 4 disappointed. Conclusion: In conclusion the study shows that injection AIT with monomeric allergoid was effective and well tolerated to the full satisfaction of the patients.

Detection of CCD in the diagnosis of sensitization to grass and weed allergens; Background: Allergy to grass and weed allergens and rhinoconjunctivitis associated with it is one of the main problems in patients with allergic pathology in different regions of Russia and most of them are recommended to carry out SCIT or SLIT. The appointment of allergen immunotherapy is advisable only after detecting true sensitization only to species-specific allergens. In the case of selective recognition of cross-reacting allergens, such as CCD and profilins, the indications for and the result of SIT are doubtful. Aim: To determine the significance of sensitization to CCD in diagnostic of sensitization to grass and weed allergens. Method: There were 1273 patients (pts) aged from 3 to 71. All sera from these pts was tested to rPhl p 1, rPhl p 5, nAmb a 1, nArt v 1 and nMUXF3 (CCD). There were 55 pts, 41 male and 14 females with sensitization to CCD and different severity of rhinoconjunctivitis observed. The presence and level of IgE-aB to by ISAC ImmunoCAP technology (Thermofisher Scientific, Sweeden). Results: For allergic components rPhl p 1, sensitization was detected in 42 (76.36%) pts, rPhl p 5 caused sensitization in 27 (49.09%) pts, to nArt v 1 in 16 (29.09%) pts and to nAmb a 1 detected in 9 (16.36%) pts. Only 2 (3.63%) pts were sensitized to all 4 components of grass and weed allergens and CCD, to 3 components in 13 pts (23.63%), 14 (25.45%) pts were sensitized to 2 components and 18 (32.72%) pts were sensitized to 1 component and 8 (14.54%) pts showed antibodies only to CCD. Conclusion: The frequency of detectable antibodies to CCD in the surveyed population is not so high 4.32% (55/1273). In most of the examined patients with sensitization to CCD, IgE-aB to grass and weed allergens was detected in 76.36%, and sensitization to CCD alone was detected in 14.54% of cases. It should be noted that of the surveyed population of patients with sensitization to grass and weed allergens IgE-aB to CCD were detected in 3.69% (47/1273). Thus, CCD may have important clinical and diagnostic significance, and their content in diagnostic extracts should be taken into account when prescribing SIT. The presence of isolated sensitivity to CCD alone can lead to misdiagnosis in the detection of reactions to all pollen allergens, which can subsequently lead to a negative result from ongoing allergen immunotherapy.
Local Type-2 Cytokines in Nasal Lining Fluids following Allergen-specific Immunotherapy; Background: Activation of Th2 cells, IgE production and eosinophilia are features of an ongoing allergic airway inflammation. This process is associated with mutual inflammatory activation between epithelium and infiltrating immune-cells. Nasal lining fluids of the upper airways could be used to monitor changes in this crosstalk during grass pollen specific immunotherapy (AIT). Method: Fifty-seven patients with allergic rhinitis were observed and biomaterials samples during the three year course of grass-pollen specific AIT. In addition, healthy controls and untreated rhinitis patients were recruited and sampled during the observational phase of the study. Nasal secretions were analyzed by electrochemiluminescence multi-array technology. Single-cell transcriptomics was used to identify source and IL-4- dependence of type-2 cytokines in IL-4- primed primary airway organoid cultures. Results: Local IL-4, as previously described, increases during updosing of AIT and decreases over the course of AIT, however not in the third year. IFN-g increased during the updosing phase as well, however showed an increase during the observational phase from year 1 to year 3. The E2-associated epithelial chemokine CCL-26 (Eotaxin-3) revealed a response upon IL-4- priming of the epithelium and was induced during pollen season, but not influenced by AIT, while IL-24 descreased following three years of AIT Periostin levels changed during the course of AIT, however influenced by the grass pollen season. In contrast, TSLP and IL-33 mainly produced by basal cells, albeit independently of IL-4, showed a seaon-independent increase in the second year out of the pollen season. Conclusion: These results demonstrate that pathological reprogramming of basal epithelial cells in terms of type-2 epithelial cytokine production seems to persist to some extent despite three years of AIT, which could potentially be one mechanism explaining why AIT only restores allergen tolerance for seven to ten years.

Sensitization profiles of individual allergic patients in Germany; Background: Several epidemiological studies have shown that polysensitization and the sensitization pattern to molecular allergens could influence in the severity of the allergic symptoms. Therefore, a better knowledge of the allergenic sensitization profile of patients in real life is needed. This information will allow a deeper understanding of the disease which could aid in the selection of the treatment. The aim of this study was to analyze the specific IgE patterns in allergic patients from Germany and to correlate with the clinical symptoms. Method: Five hundred allergic patients from different regions of Germany were included in the study. The diagnosis of allergy was based on case history, clinical allergic signs (allergic rhinitis and/or bronchial asthma) and data of skin prick-tests to aeroallergens. Sera samples were collected and analyzed by ImmunoCAP® to determine the specific IgE levels to 16 main allergenic sources (grass, weed and tree pollen, as well as, animal epithelia, moulds and house dust mites). Finally, and depending on the screening results, sIgE to other related allergenic sources and a total of 43 molecular allergens were also tested. All data collected were processed and statistically analyzed by R software. Results: All the patients were diagnosed with rhinitis and 12% also showed bronchial asthma. Regarding the sensitization profiles, 77% were sensitized to two or more allergenic sources and 23% were monosensitized to one allergenic source. Betula alba pollen was the most common cause of sensitization (59%), followed by Phleum pratense (58%). Interestingly, sensitization against animal epithelia ranked third with a 56% of the total population. The frequency of allergic individuals sensitized to the major birch pollen allergen (Bet v 1) was the highest (82%), followed by Phl p 1 and Phl p 5 (79% and 55%, respectively). However, sensitization to major allergens from Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus, Der p 1 and Der p 2, was higher than the main animal epithelia allergens tested. A positive statistically significant association was found between the severity of rhinitis symptoms and the levels of sIgE to 11 allergenic sources and 13 molecular allergens. Conclusion: We obtained a complete sensitization map in different areas from Germany, with global and individualized information on polysensitization to different allergenic sources and molecular allergens. This type of study deepens in the clinical relevance of allergens and their importance for personalized immunotherapy.

We hypothesized that PQ Grass 27,600 SU induces local (nasal mucosa) and systemic (serum) allergen-specific IgA1, IgA2, IgG and IgG4 antibodies and that the induction of these blocking antibodies correlates with the binding of allergen-IgE complexes to CD23 on B cells. Method: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled field study was performed and study participants either received injections of PQ Grass with a cumulative dose of 27,600 SU (AIT) or placebo containing MCT (PL-MCT) or saline (PL-saline). Similarly, induction of grass pollen-specific IgG and IgG4 in sera was observed at V12 (p < 0.001) and V15 (p < 0.001) compared to V1 in the AIT-treated group compared to placebo. An induction of grass pollen-specific IgG and IgG4 was observed in the local target organ (nasal mucosa). Allergen-IgE complexes binding to B cells were significantly decreased in serum at both V12 (p < 0.05) and V15 (p < 0.05) and in nasal fluid at V15 (p < 0.01) compared to V1 in the AIT-treated group, but not placebo. Identification of candidate transcriptome biomarkers from peripheral blood mononuclear cells for monitoring of clinical efficacy of grass subcutaneous immunotherapy; Background: A modified 13-grass allergen subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) product (PQ Grass) using MicroCrystalline Tyrosine (MCT) and Monophosphoryl Lipid A (MPL) as an adjuvant system was evaluated in an exploratory field trial. One of the aims of the clinical trial was to elucidate grass SCIT-induced molecular mechanisms and identify potential transcriptome biomarkers of efficacy and clinical monitoring following completion of the conventional treatment at the start and at the end of the Grass Pollen Season (GPS). Method: A randomised double-blind placebo-controlled field trial to explore the efficacy and safety of PQ Grass 27600 SU in 119 adult subjects with seasonal allergic rhinoconjunctivitis to grass pollen was completed. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) samples for RT2 Profiler PCR Array gene expression analysis were collected at Visit 1 (baseline), Visit 12 (pre-GPS) ≈1-5 weeks after last injection and Visit 15 (post-GPS). A panel of 58 genes focused on basophils, T helper cell Type 1 (Th1)/ T helper cell Type 2 (Th2)/allergen-specific Th2 (Th2A), T regulatory cell (Treg), B cells and dendritic cells (DCs) was analysed and fold change calculated (ΔΔCt method). Statistical significance was determined using Student's t test and power analysis was performed to calculate minimum samples size per group to validate the results from the current dataset. Results: Transcriptome analysis of active treatment (conventional posology) vs placebo with MCT identified clusters of differentially expressed genes related to upregulation of Th1/Treg and downregulation of Th2/Th2A canonical pathways. Changes in expression level of corresponding transcription factors will be presented. Conclusion: A distinct profile of SCIT-induced responses from grass-allergic subjects enrolled in an exploratory field study with PQ Grass revealed clusters of related genes associated with suppression of type 2 immunity and immune deviation towards Th1 responses compared to placebo. Several differentially expressed transcriptome biomarkers could be considered as surrogate biomarkers for subsequent clinical trials based on the additional data acquired using power analysis tools.

Intralymphatic immunotherapy of patients using a modified MicroCrystalline tyrosine absorbed grass product: A dbpc RCT; Background: Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) by the intralymphatic route (ILIT) has been studied for about 15 years in more than a dozen small trials and is currently subject of the large clinical trial ILIT.NU (EudraCT 2020-001060- 28). Common for most of these studies was that native allergen adjuvanted with aluminium hydroxide was administered. The aim of the current clinical trial is to study ILIT using a modified grass product adjuvanted with the biodegradable depot MicroCrystalline Tyrosine (modified allergen MCT absorbed, MATA). Method: Patients with allergic rhinitis due to sensitisation to grass pollen allergens were recruited in Switzerland through online and social media, flyers, and email to University employees. Subsequent to an online screening (www.ILIT.NU), onsite screening included sixty study participants that were randomized to receive ILIT with MATA (n = 30) or with placebo (n = 30). Three ultrasound-guided ILIT injections of 100 mcl into an inguinal lymph node were given on four-week intervals, and the dose administered was 1/15th of the recommended maintenance dose utilized for subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT). ILIT-associated adverse events (AEs) were recorded for three days after each injection using an online application. Results: The recruitment method was effective and enabled inclusion and treatment of 60 patients within four weeks of final approval by the ethics and medical agency on January 27th 2022. Online screening started on January 28th 2022, and first patient was treated on February 10th 2022. The ultrasound guidance ILIT procedure was fast, the time with the treating clinician being approx. 10 minutes. The 60 minutes post-treatment observation after first ILIT injection revealed mild AEs in 13 out of 60 participants (22%) and only one (1.7%) moderate AE. The moderate AE and almost all mild AEs were erythema or swelling at the site of injection. No further AEs were reported for the next three days. The injections were never associated with pain. Conclusion: Ultrasound-guided intralymphatic injection of a commercial AIT product proved safe and easy to perform. Further testing of will include clinical efficacy by a combined symptom-medication score (primary), immunological effects by antibody measurement and T-cell assays.
Role of major allergens and panallergens in ragweed (Ambrosia artemisiifolia) allergy diagnosis; Background: Ragweed allergy is considered a major health problem worldwide and identification of the molecules inducing allergic symptoms is crucial. Therefore, singleplex or multiplex platforms for the detection of specific IgE (sIgE) towards allergens have become available for in vitro allergy diagnosis. Our aim was to investigate sensitization profiles among ragweed-allergic patients in order to identify genuine ragweed sensitization to further direct allergen-specific immunotherapy (AIT) recommendations. Method: 150 patients were selected based on case history, positive skin prick test (SPT) and/or sIgE to ragweed pollen. Results: Response towards the tested major allergens revealed primary ragweed sensitization for more than half (56%) of the patients, whereas the rest showed sensitization towards at least one other major pollen allergen. One fifth of the patients (21%) appeared to be sensitized to tested profilins and in all cases inhibition experiments showed Amb a 8 inhibited IgE binding by 70-100% towards the other profilins. Furthermore, RBL assay showed both Amb a 8 and Art v 4 were able to induce degranulation in ragweed allergic patients. Conclusion: More than one third of ragweed-allergic patients showed genuine multiple sensitizations. In case of multiple reactivities due to panallergens, ImmunoCAP provided an invaluable tool in distinguishing primary sensitization from cross-reactivities. Weed profilins have proven to be clinically relevant and should be included in diagnosis work-up for increased accuracy.

Sublingual allergen immunotherapy: Safety, adherence, efficacy in adolescents during COVID-19 pandemic; Background: Allergic rhinitis, one of the most common chronic allergic diseases, commonly associated with asthma, has a disease modifying therapy, allergen-specific immunotherapy (AIT). AIT can play a significant role in the reduction of clinical and immunological reaction to the culprit allergen, decreasing the onset of new sensitizations, preventing the onset of asthma, and reducing use of pharmacological treatments. This latter aspect is highly relevant for adolescents, a category of patients that frequently prefer to use “as few drugs as possible”. AIT continuation may be difficult in some situations, such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Difficulty in accessing hospitals was experienced by many leading to a discontinuation of therapies for chronic conditions, such as allergic rhinitis. Method: We report our experience on the management, safety and adherence to sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) prescribed to 25 adolescents affected by allergic rhinitis (house dust mite (HDM) -8 patients, SLIT grass pollen -12 patients, SLIT parietaria -5 patients), during the COVID-19 pandemic, following EAACI recommendations. The first administration of SLIT was carried out under medical supervision. We used a personalized monitoring approach according to the type of SLIT prescribed and according to the needs presented by each patient, advising them how to recognize and manage a possible reaction. Results: No immediate severe adverse reactions were reported by patients. Between the 2nd and 5th day of SLIT, 4 patients in therapy with HDM SLIT, experienced an exacerbation of rhinitis symptoms, with resolution after the use of oral antihistamine and topical cortisone+antihistamine before taking the daily dose of SLIT (for 30 days). Two patients on grass pollen SLIT and 2 patients on HDM SLIT, with gastric upset after taking SLIT daily while fasting, presented a resolution of the symptom after we advised them to take the daily dose in the morning after breakfast. Five patients interrupted SLIT for COVID-19 infection, until complete resolution. To date, all 25 patients are continuing SLIT, with good tolerability, with an improvement of rhinitis symptoms. Conclusion: We have reported real-life SLIT adherence and safety in adolescents that started SLIT during the COVID-19 pandemic to confirm how SLIT is a winning strategy and the only modifying treatment for allergic conditions.
Vast majority of European patients with respiratory allergy can be managed with allergy immunotherapy for grass, birch, and house dust mite; Background: Respiratory allergy in Europe is often caused by three allergen groups: Pooideae (temperate grass family), Betulaceae (birch tree family), and Dermatophagoides species (house dust mite, HDM). Within Europe an estimated 52%, 33%, and 49% of patients with respiratory allergy have disease due to grass, tree, or HDM, respectively (Bauchau et al. 2004). The aim of this analysis was to investigate if these three allergens are similarly predominant when evaluating the proportion of patients with moderate-to- severe respiratory allergy requiring treatment with allergy immunotherapy (AIT). Method: The proportion of patients requiring AIT to treat respiratory allergy due to grass, birch tree family, or HDM were calculated based on market data. Data comprised of ALK 2021 sales data (ALK-Abelló A/S, Denmark) that were extrapolated to calculate proportions for an entire country based on market share information. Data from 14 countries were assessed to determine an estimate for the European region (AT, CH, CZ, DE, ES, DK, FI, FR, IT, NL, NO, SE, SK, UK). For some countries exact patient number data were obtained. If patient number data were not available, this number was calculated based on amount of product dispensed. Proportions are presented as a range to account for the two different methodologies employed. As an individual patient may be treated with more than one AIT product simultaneously, an adjustment was made based on the assumption that 30% of patients received >1 AIT offering. Subcutaneous and sublingual immunotherapy preparations were included in the analysis. Results: Of all aeroallergen AIT preparations utilised for treatment, grass constituted an estimated 32%-35%, birch tree family 25%-29%, and HDM 30%-32%. When corrected for AIT co-administration the proportion of patients whose AIT requirements could be met with these three allergens alone was 87.8%-88.1%. The proportion was highest for Germany and Northern Europe (DE, DK, FI, NO, SE combined) at 94-96%, and lowest for France and Southern Europe (ES, FR, IT combined) at 75-78%. Conclusion: Over 85% of patients with respiratory allergy in Europe that require AIT can be managed with a portfolio consisting of grass, birch tree family, and HDM allergen preparations. However, strategies still need to be considered to ensure availability of rarer allergens, especially in Southern Europe.
Single cell transcriptomics identify specific expression pattern specific for human regulatory B cells during grass pollen-specific immunotherapy; Background: Studies described a marked increase in IL-10+ regulatory B cells (Bregs) with a concomitant decrease in Breg-suppressed pro-inflammatory Th17 cells during the updosing injections of allergen-specific immunotherapy (AIT). Since this evidence suggests an important function of IL-10+ Bregs in the initial mechanisms of tolerance re-induction during AIT, this study aimed to substantiate this hypothesis through deep phenotype characterization of this cell population at the single-cell level. Method: PBMCs were extracted from blood samples from 12 patients with grass pollen allergy collected at baseline and 6 h after the last top dose injection during the updosing phase of grass pollen-specific immunotherapy. To characterize human IL-10+ regulatory B cells, single cell mRNA sequencing analyzes of enriched B cells from 3 patients were performed for both time points. Flow cytometry was used to validate the transcriptomic results at the single cell protein level in IL-10+ versus IL-10- CD19+ B cells from 11 patients. Results: The results of this study show the transcriptome of IL10-expressing regulatory B cells compared to B cells with no detected IL10 transcripts. In this analysis, the transcripts of the B-cell activation markers CD25, CD58, CD70, CD83, and CD86 were enriched in the IL10-expressing Breg population compared to the IL10-negative B cells. In the subsequent single-cell protein analysis using flow cytometry, this enrichment was found in CD19+IL-10+ versus CD19+IL-10- confirmed as significantly increased. In addition, the well-known Breg marker CD24 was significantly increased at the protein level. However, one result in particular stood out. The regulatory T-cell transcription factor FoxP3 was also increased at the protein level in CD19+IL-10+, but here the IL-10+ B-cell population was divided into FoxP3-positive and FoxP3-negative Bregs. Interestingly, only the expression of CD86, one of the identified B-cell activation markers, changed during the AIT updosing phase. IL10+ Bregs expressed significantly less CD86 on their surface than IL10+ Bregs at baseline 6 h after the last top dose. Conclusion: This study describes the discovery of a specific immune factor expression pattern that distinguishes IL-10- positive Bregs from IL-10- negative non-regulatory B cells. In particular, it sheds light on the activation state of Bregs during the updosing phase of AIT and on regulatory phenotype-promoting molecules that may underlie the Breg phenotype.

Efficacy and safety of sublingual immunotherapy for allergic rhinitis: A network meta-analysis; Background: To systematically evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of sublingual immunotherapy for allergic rhinitis (AR) and provide evidence for clinical treatment. Methods: A literature search was performed on the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang database, PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Embase database. Data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of sublingual immunotherapy for AR were screened and extracted from the establishment of those databases to November 2022. Subsequently, a network meta-analysis was performed using a statistical software R 4.2. Results: Totally 22 RCTs that met the inclusion and exclusion criteria and screened from 1,164 literature were included. A total of 4,941 AR patients were involved in the 22 trials, as well as five interventions including placebo, pharmacotherapy, subcutaneous immunotherapy_dust mite, sublingual immunotherapy_dust mite, and sublingual immunotherapy_ grass mix plus pollen extract. The results of network meta-analysis showed that, based on symptom scores after different interventions for AR, the most effective treatments for AR were in order as follows: sublingual immunotherapy_dust mite, subcutaneous immunotherapy_dust mite, sublingual immunotherapy_ grass mix plus pollen extract, placebo, and pharmacotherapy. Importantly, sublingual immunotherapy had fewer adverse reactions and higher safety. Conclusion: Sublingual immunotherapy_dust mite for AR has the best efficacy, whereas traditional medicine has the worst. More high-quality studies with a large sample and multiple centers are needed to verify this conclusion in the future, so as to further provide more reliable evidence-based medical evidence for the clinical treatment options of AR patients.

Off-label Use of Oral Immunotherapy for Rhinoconjunctivitis and Asthma due to Grass Pollen: A Safe and Effective Alternative in Patients over 65 Years Old: A Series of Case Reports; Introduction: Allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and asthma are the most common IgE-mediated diseases worldwide. Allergen-specific immunotherapy (AIT) is currently the only modifying treatment for these IgE-mediated diseases in both children and adults. Subcutaneous immunotherapy is widely used, but in patients over 65 years old, there may be an increased risk of adverse reactions and a worse response to treatment. Oral immunotherapy (OIT) has been proven to be effective and safe, but currently, in most countries, it has been licensed only for patients up to 65 years old based on its technical datasheet. So far, no studies on the efficacy and safety of this type of immunotherapy in patients older than 65 years old have been published. Case Presentation: We present four patients older than 65 years old with a diagnosis of moderate seasonal rhinoconjunctivitis and moderate-persistent seasonal pollen-induced asthma. Off-label use of oral immunotherapy (OIT) for grass pollen was prescribed due to the severity of their rhinocon-junctivitis symptoms and the worsening of asthma symptoms during the spring. Improvement in the rhinoconjunctivitis and asthma symptoms was reported by all patients since the first spring season and was maintained during the following two years of follow-up. There were no systemic reactions, and only two patients initially had self-limiting oral pruritus. Conclusion: Oral immunotherapy for pollens appears to be a convenient, effective, and safe option in older patients (>65 years) with comorbidities after a three-year treatment. This is, to the best of our knowledge, the first report on the off-label use of OIT in patients over 65 years old with symptoms of allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and asthma.
Pharmacotherapy and immunotherapy of allergic rhinitis induced by house dust mite, grass, and birch pollen allergens: a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials; Background: The aim of this study was to assess the efficacy and safety of oral antihistamines (AHs), intranasal antihistamines (INAH) intranasal glucocorticosteroids (INCS), subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT), and sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) in the management of allergic rhinitis (AR). The authors focused on the division into selected AR’s triggers: house dust mites (HDMs), grass pollen, and birch pollen. Methods: For each drug and allergen class, a meta-analysis of the efficacy and adverse events (AEs) was performed. The obtained results were presented as a therapeutic index (TIX-Score). Results: Twenty-seven randomized clinical trials (RCTs) were included. The best total efficacy was observed for: HDMs for INCS and grass pollen for combination of INCS with INAH in a single device and for INAH. Considering the data that was obtained for birch pollen, SLIT showed statistically significant total efficacy. Summation scores for efficacy and AEs showed highest TIX-Score for combination of INCS and INAH in a single device in grass pollen. Conclusions: Treatment methods selected for this review may serve as an effective and safe treatment in reducing perennial and seasonal AR’s symptoms. However, due to high heterogeneity probably associated with potential confounders existence in control in some cases, results should be interpreted with caution.
Evaluation of Intralymphatic Immunotherapy in Allergic Rhinitis Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis; Background. Intralymphatic immunotherapy (ILIT) is short-course administration of allergen-specific immunotherapy (AIT). This study is aimed at assessing the clinical efficacy and safety of ILIT in patients with allergic rhinitis (AR). Methods. MEDLINE, PUBMED, and Cochrane Library were used to conduct electronic searches for clinical trials comparing ILIT and placebo in patients with AR. The final search took place on August 24, 2022. Local swelling or erythema was the main AE following injection (random effects model, RD 0.16, 95% CI [0.05, 0.27], P=0.005). Discussion. For individuals with AR, ILIT is safe and effective. ILIT alleviates clinical symptoms and reduces pharmaceutical consumption without causing severe AEs. However, the validity of this study is compromised by the substantial heterogeneity and risk of bias in the included researches. RegistrationCRD42022355329.

The aim of this study was to determine the distribution of specific IgE antibodies to major and minor birch pollen allergens in a population of allergic Norwegian individuals by using a birch allergic blood donor population as a surrogate sample. Sixty blood donors were recruited and sampled based on birch allergy symptoms such as rhinitis, rhinoconjunctivitis and/or mild asthma in previous seasons. All sera were collected before start of the pollen season and tested using a line blot assay (Euroimmun AG, Lübeck, Germany) for IgE to birch and timothy pollen. Both extracts, single allergens, and cross-reacting carbohydrate determinants (CCD) were analysed. Only donors with specific IgE to birch and/or timothy grass were further evaluated. Specific IgE to birch pollen extract was found in 52 sera, and sensitization to timothy grass in 40 sera. Specific IgE to Bet v 1 was predominant in contrast to Bet v 4 which was absent. However, sensitization to the minor allergens Bet v 2 and 6 was always found together with high levels of IgE to Bet v 1. Subjects sensitized to the profilin Bet v 2 from birch were also sensitized to Phl p 12 from timothy grass. In conclusion, there was predominantly Bet v 1 sensitization in this cohort and low sensitization to minor allergens and cross-reactive allergens (Bet v 2, Bet v 4, Phl p 7 and Phl p 12).

A 5-Year Open-Label Follow-up of a Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Trial of Intralymphatic Immunotherapy for Birch and Grass Allergy Reveals Long-term Beneficial Effects; Background: Intralymphatic immunotherapy (ILIT) is a novel, faster alternative to conventional allergen immunotherapy (AIT). Few previous studies have evaluated its long-term effects. The objective of the present study was to complete a 5-year follow-up of a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of ILIT for a combination of birch and grass allergens. Methods: Fifty-eight patients with allergic rhinitis were treated with either placebo or a combination of ALK Alutard Birch and Grass 1000 SQ-U administered in 3 intralymphatic injections at 1-month intervals. A year after the vaccination, the symptoms induced by nasal provocation were significantly reduced. After 5-6 years, 20 out of 26 actively treated patients were followed up with a nasal provocation test (NPT) and seasonal registration of the combined symptom and medications score (CSMS), IgE and IgG4 levels in blood, and immunological markers in blood and lymph nodes and compared with 13 unvaccinated controls. Results: The reduction in the NPT response with ILIT at year 1 could not be convincingly reproduced at year 5. The new CSMS scores were markedly lower among the previously treated patients than among the control group. Furthermore, grass-specific IgG4 was increased, grass-specific IgE decreased, FcεR1 on basophils was reduced, and the fraction of memory T-cells in lymph nodes increased. Conclusion: The combination of seasonal clinical data and immunological parameters supports the notion of a long-lasting effect of ILIT. These data support the concept of ILIT as a good alternative to traditional AIT in pollen-induced allergic rhinitis.
Adoptive transfer of allergen-expressing B cells prevents IgE-mediated allergy; Introduction: Prophylactic strategies to prevent the development of allergies by establishing tolerance remain an unmet medical need. We previously reported that the transfer of autologous hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) expressing the major timothy grass pollen allergen, Phl p 5, on their cell surface induced allergen-specific tolerance in mice. In this study, we investigated the ability of allergen-expressing immune cells (dendritic cells, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, and CD19+ B cells) to induce allergen-specific tolerance in naive mice and identified CD19+ B cells as promising candidates for allergen-specific cell therapy. Methods: For this purpose, CD19+ B cells were isolated from Phl p 5-transgenic BALB/c mice and transferred to naive BALB/c mice, pre-treated with a short course of rapamycin and an anti-CD40L antibody. Subsequently, the mice were subcutaneously sensitized three times at 4-week intervals to Phl p 5 and Bet v 1 as an unrelated control allergen. Allergen-expressing cells were followed in the blood to monitor molecular chimerism, and sera were analyzed for Phl p 5- and Bet v 1-specific IgE and IgG1 levels by RBL assay and ELISA, respectively. In vivo allergen-induced lung inflammation was measured by whole-body plethysmography, and mast cell degranulation was determined by skin testing. Results: The transfer of purified Phl p 5-expressing CD19+ B cells to naive BALB/c mice induced B cell chimerism for up to three months and prevented the development of Phl p 5-specific IgE and IgG1 antibody responses for a follow-up period of 26 weeks. Since Bet v 1 but not Phl p 5-specific antibodies were detected, the induction of tolerance was specific for Phl p 5. Whole-body plethysmography revealed preserved lung function in CD19+ B cell-treated mice in contrast to sensitized mice, and there was no Phl p 5-induced mast cell degranulation in treated mice. Discussion: Thus, we demonstrated that the transfer of Phl p 5-expressing CD19+ B cells induces allergen-specific tolerance in a mouse model of grass pollen allergy. This approach could be further translated into a prophylactic regimen for the prevention of IgE-mediated allergy in humans.

Subgroup analysis was further conducted in terms of study design [randomized controlled trials (RCTs), cohort studies], allergen [house dust mites (HDMs), grass pollen], treatment duration (≥ 24, 12-23 or < 12 months), allergen immunotherapy (AIT) modality (drops or tablets), and AIT protocol [continuous, pre-seasonal, co-seasonal, or after the grass pollen season (GPS)]. Sensitivity analysis was conducted for all outcomes. A Bayesian framework and a Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) model were developed for indirect comparison. Results: Totally 50 studies with 10813 AR children were included, with 4122 treated with SLIT, 1852 treated with SCIT, and 4839 treated with non-SLIT or non-SCIT therapy. Care with allergen immunotherapy for allergic respiratory diseases in Germany—Predictors and deficits; Background: Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) represents the only possibility of causal therapy for allergic respiratory diseases. Although the prevailing high prevalence of allergic diseases and restrictions in the daily lives of patients, AIT is offered to a suboptimal number of patients in Germany. Methods: Insured patients with documented allergic respiratory disease of one of the largest statutory health insurances in Germany, ‘DAK-Gesundheit’, were contacted by postal mail and asked to participate in the study. In case of written consent, primary and secondary data of patients were collected and analysed. Patient characteristics, predictors of being offered AIT, predictors of performing AIT and guideline-compliant care were analysed. Results: 2505 subjects were included in the VerSITA study. Allergy to tree pollen and native speaking were identified as predictors, which increase the probability of being offered AIT. The probability was significantly decreased by the characteristics allergic rhinitis only, allergic asthma only, age in years, non-German citizenship, no graduation and lower secondary qualification. Significant positive predictors for an AIT to be actually performed were: Allergy to tree pollen and male sex. Predictors that decrease the likelihood that AIT is performed were: only allergic asthma, current smoker, former smoker, age and non-German citizenship. Furthermore, it was possible to identify characteristics in which guideline-compliant patients differed significantly from the rest of the study population. Conclusions: Based on statutory health insurance data and patient survey data, the VerSITA study provides a broad and in-depth overview of the care situation with regard to AIT in Germany and identifies deficits.

ELEVATED BASELINE SERUM TRYPTASE AND HEREDITARY ALPHA TRYPTASEMIA (HAT); Introduction: Hereditary alpha tryptasemia (HaT) is an autosomal dominant genetic trait characterized by elevated basal serum tryptase levels due to extra allelic copies of the tryptase alpha/beta 1 (TPSAB1) gene. HaT has been associated with multisystem complaints and as a modifier of mast cell-associated disorders and anaphylaxis. Case Description: A 38-year-old male presented for evaluation of food and environmental allergies. He had severe oropharyngeal symptoms and a throat-closing sensation immediately after ingesting raw fruits and tree nuts. He also had symptoms of perennial allergic rhinoconjunctivitis with seasonal variation. Allergy skin testing showed IgE sensitivities to tree, grass and weed pollens, dust mites, mold spores, cat, dog, and cockroach. He had no IgE sensitivities to any of the fruits tested. He had IgE sensitivities to walnut, hazelnut, and almond. Given the severity of his oropharyngeal symptoms a baseline serum tryptase was checked, which was elevated at 20.3 mcg/L. Repeat determinations again showed baseline serum tryptase above 20 mcg/L. CBC with differential and CMP were within normal limits. 24-hour urinary histamine and N-methylhistamine were both within normal. Kit D16 mutation analysis was negative. TPSAB1 copy number analysis showed extra allelic alpha-tryptase copies, consistent with hereditary alpha tryptasemia (HaT). The patient received counseling and standard treatment for environmental/food allergies and tolerates allergen-specific immunotherapy. Discussion: HaT is an inherited condition considered a biochemical trait and can be present in around 5% of the general population. Patients with elevated baseline serum tryptase may benefit from testing for extra allelic copies of TPSAB1.
ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS INFLUENCING SYMPTOMS AND USE OF RELIEF MEDICATIONS IN SUBJECTS WITH SEASONAL ALLERGIC RHINOCONJUNCTIVITIS; Introduction: In Phase III Allergen Immunotherapy (AIT) trials, the underlying assumption is that there is a causal relation between symptoms and allergen burden. However, there is a more complex interplay of allergen exposure and environmental variables. We report on a study where the impact of environmental factors has prospectively been taken into account to evaluate their impact on AIT treatment effects. Methods: An exploratory field study comparing the efficacy of a modified grass subcutaneous immunotherapy product using MCT and MPL as adjuvant system (PQ Grass) versus placebo in subjects with allergic rhinitis/rhinoconjunctivitis was performed. The combined symptom and medication score (CSMS) during the peak grass pollen season was the primary endpoint. The daily pollen exposure as well as daily ozone and humidity levels were also collected. An exploratory analysis was defined using a hierarchical linear mixed model to evaluate the influence of these environmental variables on the primary endpoint results using observed cases. Results: A statistically significant influence of daily humidity (p<0.001) in addition to the daily pollen burden on CSMS was demonstrated. When correcting the primary endpoint for these environmental factors the average CSMS improvement after PQ grass compared to placebo improved from 39.5% (based on the primary analysis model) without adjustment for environmental factors to 55.6% with adjustment (p<0.001) (observed cases). Conclusion: Environmental conditions have an influence on the severity of the CSMS and correcting for these influences by introducing these as covariates may improve the primary outcome of Phase III AIT field studies.
IMMUNOMODULATORY MECHANISMS OF GRASS ALLERGEN IMMUNOTHERAPY ON DIFFERENTIAL T CELLS TRANSCRIPTOME POLARIZATION IN EXPLORATORY TRIAL; Introduction: A short pre-seasonal course of grass subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) using MicroCrystalline Tyrosine (MCT) and Monophosphoryl Lipid A showed a significant improvement in combined symptom and medication scores (CSMS) in an exploratory field study (PQGrass309). Moreover, molecular mechanisms associated clinical benefit remain to be fully determined. Methods: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were obtained from participants, who underwent subcutaneous grass immunotherapy or placebo with MCT at baseline, end of treatment and end of grass pollen season (GPS). A panel of 58 genes was profiled. Ingenuity Pathway Analysis was deployed to elucidate molecular signature and functional relationships for observed gene expression. Results: CSMS was significantly decreased (-33%) following grass SCIT compared to placebo with MCT. Transcriptome profiling showed transient upregulation of Th2/Th2A and Th17 signature cytokines at the start of GPS and steady downregulation at the end of GPS. Immune modulation towards Th1/Treg at pre-GPS and post-GPS with upregulation of IFNγ, IL-12A, EBI3 (IL-35), IL-27, IL-10, TGFβ was indicative of immune tolerance induction. T helper cell differentiation was one of the most significantly enriched pathways with Th17 mapped as a top enriched canonical pathway, which was transiently upregulated at the start of GPS and downregulated at the end of GPS. Upstream regulator analysis predicted IL-4, IL17A/IL17F, IL-13 and IFNγ as top upstream regulators at pre-GPS and IFNγ, IL-12A, IL-27 at post-GPS. Conclusion: A distinct immunomodulatory profile of grass SCIT induced responses revealed clusters of differentially expressed genes, which supports restoration of the Th1/Th2 balance and provides the underpinning mechanisms associated with the robust clinical efficacy outcome.

Allergen immunotherapy for allergic airway diseases: Use lessons from the past to design a brighter future; Allergic respiratory diseases, such as allergic dermatitis, food allergy, allergic rhino conjunctivitis and allergic asthma, are chronic inflammatory diseases with increasing prevalence. Symptoms include such as watery or itchy itching of the mouth, skin, or the eyes, swelling of the face or throat, sneezing, congestion or vomiting, wheezing, shortness of breath and coughing. For allergic asthma, additional symptoms include tightness of chest, cough, wheezing, and reversible airflow limitation. These symptoms can be triggered by inhalation of allergens such as food allergens or airborne allergens such as those from tree- or grass pollen and house dust mites. Pharmacological intervention in allergic disease includes the use of antihistamines, immune suppressive drugs and in case of asthma, the use of (long acting) beta-agonists for relaxation of the constricted airways. These treatment options merely suppress symptoms and do not cure the disease. Allergen immunotherapy (AIT), in contrast, has the capacity of inducing long-term tolerance, with symptom relief persisting decennia after discontinuation of treatment, despite recurrent re-exposure to the allergen. However, AIT is not effective for all allergic disorders, and treatment for several years is required to obtain long-term protection. Moreover, some forms of AIT have safety concerns, with risk of mild to severe allergic reactions. To improve safety and efficacy of AIT, the underlying mechanisms have been studied extensively in the clinic as well as in experimental models of allergic airway inflammation. Despite more than a century of clinical experience and a vast body of experimental and translational studies into the immunological and cellular mechanisms underpinning its therapeutic potential, AIT is still not implemented in routine clinical care for allergic asthma. This review provides an overview of the substantial developments that contribute to our knowledge of the pathogenesis of allergic airway diseases, the mechanism of action of AIT, its treatment routes and schedules, the standardization of extracts and use of adjuvantia. Moreover, the main conclusions from experimental models of AIT with regard to the safety and effectiveness of the treatment are summarized, and future directions for further improvements are outlined. AIT urgently requires further improvements in order to increase its efficiency and shorten the treatment duration while remaining safe and cost-effective.
Pre-treatment allergen-specific IgE analysis and outcomes of allergen immunotherapy; Background. Patients show varied results to allergen immunotherapy (AIT). Does allergen immunotherapy for allergic rhinitis prevent asthma?; Asthma and allergic rhinitis (AR) have overlapping clinical and pathologic features, sustained by an underlying T helper 2 bias, resulting in airway inflammation that extends from the nose to the lung. Children who are monosensitized often develop polysensitization over time, and they are at high risk of developing asthma. The effect of allergen immunotherapy (AIT) is allergen specific, resulting in symptom improvement and reduction in medication requirement. It is the only known treatment that alters the natural history of allergic disease and induces long-term remission. A bystander or allergen-nonspecific effect of AIT has also been proposed—that AIT to 1 allergen might reduce the risk of development of sensitization to other allergens. Furthermore, several observational studies and clinical trials, in seasonal (pollen) and perennial (house dust mite) AR, have investigated a protective effect of AIT to prevent asthma. The overall evidence favors an asthma preventive effect of AIT in AR to grass and birch tree pollen. Fewer studies have investigated the use of AIT in children with perennial AR due to house dust mite allergy to prevent asthma, and the results are less convincing. The use of AIT to reduce the risk of progression to asthma, in children with AR, potentially has high impact, and it will make AIT more attractive and cost-effective. However, most studies have been of small sample size or of poor design, using different allergens and AIT methodology, making it challenging to draw firm conclusions. There is a need to do adequately powered studies with optimal design and assess cost-effectiveness of this strategy.
Allergen Immunotherapy in Young Children; Purpose of Review: Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) has been shown to be safe and effective in children and is a unique treatment strategy that has disease-modifying and preventative effects that are not shared with other treatment options for allergic diseases. This article reviews the present knowledge and relevant updates on AIT in children. Recent Findings: Although there is no definite lower age limit for starting AIT, clear indications for AIT are established and each case should be considered individually by weighing risks and benefits. Documented short- and long-term benefits of AIT in children with allergic disease include significant improvement of symptoms and quality of life, and decreased use of medications as well as preventing the development of new allergen sensitizations and the progression of allergic rhinitis to asthma. Summary: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the present knowledge and key updates on AIT in the pediatric population.

Methods: A total of 88 subjects aged 18-52 years with SAR were enrolled and randomized into the SLIT group and control group. Conclusions: This study proved that A. annua-SLIT can provide equivalent efficacy and safety for SAR patients under the circumstance of accepting the pre-seasonal treatment of 8-9 or 12-13 weeks, regardless of monosensitization or polysensitization.
Conjunctival allergen provocation tests in children -A real life study; Objectives: Conjunctival allergen provocation test (CPT) is a safe and informative tool to assess systemic and local IgE-mediated ocular allergy, although it is currently underused in clinical practice, particularly in pediatric age. Our aim was to assess the safety and efficacy of CPT in children with rhinoconjunctivitis. Method: Longitudinal assessment of 87 patients (75.6% males, mean age 11.2 years [minimum 4 and maximum 17]) followed in a Portuguese allergy department between July 2016 and December 2021 and referred to CPT due to discrepancies between clinical history and allergen sensitization profile, to assess local IgE-mediated allergy or to guide allergen immunotherapy. Ocular symptoms were present in 69% of children, characterized by itching, hyperemia, tearing or chemosis. CPT were conducted accordingly to the guidelines with Leti® allergen extracts of Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus (Dp) and grass pollen mix (Dactylis, Festuca, Lolium, Phleum and Poa). Challenges were classified using Total Ocular Symptom Score (TOSS) and all patients were observed at least 2 hours after the procedure. Results: A total of 131 CPTs were performed, 75 with Dp extract and 56 with grass pollen mix. Positivity was present in 78.7% and 64.3% of CPT, with a mean (standard deviation [SD]) TOSS of 6.0 (0.9) and 5.9 (0.8) for Dp extract and grass pollen, respectively. Positive CPT required topical antihistamine in 72.5% of cases and topical corticosteroid in 9.9%, with no systemic or late phase reactions reported. Local allergic rhinoconjunctivitis to Dp was diagnosed in one patient and 36 children began allergen immunotherapy after conducting CPT. Conclusions: CPT showed to be a feasible and safe tool to assess children with rhinoconjunctivitis that presented inconsistence between clinic and sensitization pattern. Further studies are needed to evaluate if it can also be used to assess efficacy of allergen immunotherapy in clinical practice.
Patients' experience and treatment effectiveness after receiving allergen immunotherapy -A real-world experience; Objectives: To review patients' experience and treatment effectiveness after receiving allergen immunotherapy (AIT) in the Adult Allergy Department at Guy's Hospital, NHS Foundation Trust, UK Method: The survey was carried out as part of an approved quality improvement project. Patient surveys were sent to all patients who completed allergen immunotherapy from 2015 to 2016 (n = 206) by post. The survey contained nine questions addressing the follow areas: treatment effectiveness, improvement of quality of life, reduced treatment (GP visit, prescription, sick leave), persistence of improvement, willingness to repeat AIT if no longer effective and whether having a good experience during the treatment. Results: Forty-seven out of 206 questionnaires (23%) were returned by post. Majority (36%) of the responders received grass and tree pollen immunotherapy, followed by bee venom (13%), grass (13%), grass, tree and house dust mite immunotherapy (13%). In total, 76% recipients received subcutaneous AIT while 24% obtained oral AIT. Out of 47 patients, nearly 90% completed 3-year treatment (n = 41). In total, 21% recalled absence from work or study due to allergen related symptoms. A median of 8 days (IQR 5-20) of absence was reported. Forty-two patients (93%) expressed they had a good experience during the treatment in our unit. Thirty-eight patients (83%) felt the treatment improved their quality of life. More than 70% of the patients felt that the treatment was effective, improved one's ability to go out with family and friends and/ or enjoy outdoor activities more, treatment is still effective and deriving benefit from treatment at the time of the survey and would undergo AIT again in future if recommended. In total 43%-57% subjects thought the AIT reduced GP visits and/or prescriptions and/or sick leaves related to the allergen(s). Conclusions: In summary, the survey results were reflective of high degree of patient satisfaction and effectiveness of treatment, which we believe, should be the objectives and benchmarks of a good immunotherapy service.
Evaluation of first dose home self-administration of Oralvac sublingual immunotherapy for allergic rhinitis in a UK Allergy centre; Objectives: The UK SPC for Oralvac sublingual immunotherapy for allergic rhinitis was updated in May 2020 to allow first dose administration at home rather than hospital only. Standard practice in the UK has been for sublingual immunotherapy products to be initiated in hospital. Due to the coronavirus pandemic and the need to reduce hospital visits, our department altered practice to allow patients to start the first dose of this treatment at home. We conducted a survey to evaluate patients' experiences and determine the feasibility and acceptability of home initiation of Oralvac sublingual immunotherapy. Method: An anonymized online survey was distributed to the thirty patients newly started on Oralvac at home by the Allergy department at Frimley Park Hospital during the coronavirus pandemic. Patients had received detailed information about the treatment prior to starting therapy. Results: There was a 73% response rate. Most patients received tree pollen (73%), followed by grass pollen (41%) and then house dust mite (23%). The majority (68.2%) preferred to receive the first dose at home as the instructions were easy to follow, it was convenient not travelling to hospital and the risk of coronavirus was reduced. Written instructions were found to be clear by 95.5%. There were no cases of anaphylaxis or severe allergic reactions to the product. All patients reported minor side effects such as oral tingling, discomfort, headache and fatigue. None felt the need to seek medical attention. Conclusions: Our data demonstrates that unsupervised first-dose home administration of Oralvac is feasible, well-accepted by patients and safe and can be undertaken in routine clinical allergy practice in the UK. Efficacy and safety of sublingual allergen immunotherapy; Sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT)-tablets represent a new allergen immunotherapy option for clinicians. In North America, there are five SLIT-tablets approved for the treatment of allergic rhinoconjunctivitis (ARC). No SLIT-drops products are currently approved in the United States or Canada. This work reviewed the efficacy of the timothy grass SLIT-tablet, five-grass SLIT-tablet, ragweed SLIT-tablet, house-dust mite SLIT-tablet, and tree SLIT-tablet in patients with ARC. All the SLIT-tablets showed consistent clinical efficacy for the treatment of ARC in large, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, including for both patients who were monosensitized and those who were polysensitized. Treatment with house-dust mite SLIT-tablet has shown efficacy in patients who are pollen sensitized during their respective pollen seasons. In contrast to SLIT-tablets, efficacy studies of SLIT-drops show high heterogeneity of treatment effect. Although data are scarce, data that compared the efficacy of SLIT-tablets versus ARC pharmacotherapy generally indicated that SLIT-tablets had a greater benefit than pharmacotherapy when compared with placebo, particularly for perennial ARC. When compared with subcutaneous immunotherapy, analysis of these data indicated that SLIT-tablets had a benefit over subcutaneous immunotherapy in regard to safety but somewhat less benefit in regard to efficacy. The safety of SLIT-tablets has been well documented, and a U.S. Food and Drug Administration class label with safety considerations is present in the prescribing information for all SLIT-tablets. No new safety signals have been observed after reinitiating SLIT-tablets after a short treatment interruption.
Long-term efficacy of the sublingual and subcutaneous routes in allergen immunotherapy; Allergen immunotherapy is highly effective in selected patients with allergic rhinitis, allergic asthma, and Hymenoptera venom allergy. Unlike anti-allergic drugs, both subcutaneous and sublingual immunotherapies have been shown to modify the underlying cause of the disease, with proved long-term clinical benefits after treatment cessation. In this review, we analyzed 10 randomized, double-blind, placebo controlled clinical trials of allergen immunotherapy that included blinded follow-up for at least 1 year after treatment withdrawal. Three studies of pollen subcutaneous immunotherapy provided evidence that a sustained, tolerogenic effect of subcutaneous immunotherapy can be achieved after 3 years of treatment. Six trials of sublingual immunotherapy provided robust evidence for long-term clinical benefit and persistent immunologic changes after grass pollen, house-dust mite, or Japanese cedar immunotherapy, whereas a clinical trial of both sublingual and subcutaneous grass pollen immunotherapies showed that 2 years of immunotherapy were efficacious but insufficient to induce long-term tolerance. These studies strongly supported international guidelines that recommend at least 3 years of allergen immunotherapy of proven value to achieve disease modification and sustained clinical and immunologic tolerance.
Integrating the evidence in allergen immunotherapy: Why real-world data should be important for the practicing clinician?; Data obtained from controlled clinical trials are the gold standard for evaluation of allergen immunotherapy (AIT) efficacy and safety. Less prone to biases (with a strong internal validity), they allow their use and external validation in the real world. The quantity and diversity of real-world data has increased exponentially, and access to large cohorts and electronic medical records have made this information increasingly accessible and useful for research and regulatory purposes. New retrospective database studies have confirmed the sustained benefits of grass, birch pollen, and house dust mite AIT for both allergic rhinitis and asthma symptom and medication scores, the prevention of asthma (when used in nonasthmatic rhinitics), and the real rate of adverse systemic reactions. They also have addressed clinical practice issues not elsewhere analyzed, including the management of polysensitized patients with respiratory allergies and adherence to AIT. Real-world evidence has its own biases and limits that need to be taken into account. In this article we present a concise summary of the literature about the role of real-world evidence in AIT.
Assessing cross-reactivity in allergen immunotherapy; Knowledge of patterns of pollen cross-reactivity is crucial for formulation of immunotherapy vaccines. As phylogenetic relationships have become better clarified through the use of tools such as gene sequencing, it is apparent that cross-reactivity reflects taxonomy in the vast majority of cases. Contradictory observations of unexpected cross-reactivity between distantly related plants require explanation. There are many proteins, presumably performing vital functions, tightly preserved throughout the evolutionary tree from plants to animals. Examples are profilins, lipid transfer proteins, and pathogenesisrelated proteins. These may function as panallergens. The small differences that exist between these ubiquitous proteins may explain why these are frequently minor allergens, not reacting in the majority of allergic sera. This article summarizes crossreactivity from older studies using crude pollen extracts as well as newer research of purified or recombinant allergenic proteins. The patterns of cross-allergenicity that emerge should be helpful in guiding therapeutic decisions.
Future directions in allergen immunotherapy; Both subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) and sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) are effective clinically against allergic rhinitis and allergic asthma, and modify the underlying immunologic abnormalities. Despite this, many patients who could benefit from receiving SCIT and SLIT do not because of concerns about safety and the inconvenience in receiving SCIT, and the long duration of treatment with both, 3-4 years being required for lasting benefit. Attempts to improve the efficacy and safety, and to shorten the course of allergen immunotherapy have taken many approaches. Some approaches have generated great enthusiasm, only to fail in larger trials and be discarded. Other approaches show some promise but perhaps not enough to achieve regulatory approval. Those approaches that seem to have the best chance of becoming available in the next few years include the following: intralymphatic and epicutaneous immunotherapy, vitamin D in patients with insufficient serum 25 hydroxy vitamin D, probiotics, and allergoids, but all require further studies before being ready for nonexperimental use or, where necessary, for regulatory approval.
